entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antonello Gagini was a prominent Italian sculptor of the Renaissance, mainly active in Sicily and Calabria, from approximately 1480 to 1536.

As a master of the Renaissance humanist style, Gagini's works exemplified the revival of classical Greek and Roman art, as seen in his intricate carvings and ornate sculptures.

One of his most notable contributions was his role in popularizing the use of white marble in sculpture, a technique he learned from his father, Giovanni Antonio Amati.

Gagini's success was also due to his connections with the powerful Italian royal family, the House of Aragon, who commissioned many of his works.

He also collaborated with other renowned artists of his time, including Donato Bramante and Francesco Pitigliani.

In addition to his artistic achievements, Gagini's legacy extends to the preservation of traditional Sicilian and Calabrian artistic techniques, passed down through generations of skilled artisans.

As a testament to his skill and artistic vision, Gagini's works continue to inspire artists and art lovers to this day.

Gagini's contributions to the world of art are a testament to the enduring power of human creativity and innovation.
